who: Keyboard users who jump by heading
takeaways: If it looks like a heading, a list, a table or a group, it must be one in code.
Heading levels describe structure, not size. Do not skip a level to get a style.
Labels are tied to their fields. Related fields are grouped under a group label.
Your layers and annotations are where this structure gets decided.
failures: Bold text used as a heading
Radio buttons with no group label
check: Outline the page using only its headings. Does it make sense?
Label each heading with its level in the file.
Check that every table has its header cells identified.

quiz.question: A card title should be smaller than the page’s H2 style. What do you specify?
options: An H4, because it is smaller
The level the structure needs, styled smaller
quiz.why: Level follows structure. Style is separate, and a good system lets you pair any level with any size.

spec: Mark heading levels on the frame.
Identify lists, tables and their header cells.
Name each field group and page region.
review: Read me the heading outline of this page.
Which groups exist visually but have no name?
Is this really a table, or a layout?
tradeoff: Visual hierarchy and document hierarchy sometimes disagree. Separate level from style. Do not pick the level that looks right.
system: Let heading components take level and size as separate properties.
pitch: Structure is how a screen reader user skims. Without it, they have to listen to everything.
